- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast growth to 1–2% per day post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model overcorrects downward; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to offset bearish sentiment.
- In high-event periods (≥18 events/30d), model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if recent sentiment is trending.
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast mean.
- In multi-event weeks (e.g., 20+ auctions), model often fails to capture event clustering; adjust forecast to reflect cumulative event impact (e.g., +0.5% per event if supply net is negative).
